description: A pharmacy makes eye cream and foot cream using two different machines, machine 1 and machine 2. Machine 1 can  make 30 ml of eye cream and 60 ml of foot cream per hour. Machine 2 can make 45 ml of eye cream and 30 ml of foot cream per hour. Furthermore, machine 1 requires 20 ml of distilled water per hour while machine 2 requires 15 ml of distilled water per hour. The pharmacy has available 1200 ml of distilled water. If the pharmacy needs to make at least 1300 ml of eye cream and 1500 ml of foot cream, how many hours should each machine be used to minimize the total time needed?

ProductionRate.definition: Amount of product p produced per hour by machine m

WaterUsage.definition: Amount of distilled water consumed per hour by machine m

TotalWaterAvailable.definition: Total amount of distilled water available

RequiredProduct.definition: Minimum required amount of product p

objective.description: "Minimize the total operating time of the machines needed to meet the required amounts of eye cream and foot cream."

constraints.description: 30 times the hours used on machine 1 plus 45 times the hours used on machine 2 must be at least 1300 ml (eye cream requirement)
60 times the hours used on machine 1 plus 30 times the hours used on machine 2 must be at least 1500 ml (foot cream requirement)
20 times the hours used on machine 1 plus 15 times the hours used on machine 2 must not exceed 1200 ml (distilled water availability constraint)
The hours used on machine 1 must be non-negative
The hours used on machine 2 must be non-negative
